shape_construction: Believable task-specific proportions, silhouettes, construction, joins and object anatomy. Generic boxes, disconnected pipes, floating parts and unclosed architectural gaps are substantive defects. Judge intended stylization, not polygon count.
materials: Appropriate authored material vocabulary, scale, surface differentiation and consistency. Default/checker surfaces, indiscriminate tiling and texture pasted over primitive geometry do not establish finish. Do not demand wear where not requested.
lighting: Exposure, readable surfaces, shadow depth, light/material relationships across all important zones. Burnt-out whites, persistent darkness, flat unreadable surfaces and pervasive glare lower quality even if objects exist.
composition: Spatial hierarchy, focal readability, coherent massing and purposeful distribution at overview, street/room and close scales. Empty space is not inherently bad; unjustified barren requested working or inhabited zones are.
detail: Meaningful task-specific equipment, furnishing and environmental detail at large/medium/small scales. Repeated colored boxes, labels and token props cannot stand in for differentiated functional objects or rich requested spaces.
style: Match the requested/reference visual language across all zones. Real environments require plausible construction and material treatment; voxel/game styles require intentional resolved abstraction. Do not penalize coherent low-poly/voxel design for not being photorealistic.
scene_coverage: Substantive realization of the public brief and reference scene extent, connected zones, context and principal architectural/environmental features. Judge the realized scene, not merely presence counts or labels. Avoid requiring identical camera or incidental photograph clutter.
functional_identity: Visible differentiation and credible furnishing of required functional areas and mechanisms. A named room with token objects is partial credit. Compare defining reference features when supplied. Do not infer actual interactive success from appearance.

formula: continuous quality anchored to visible completion; coverage and deviation retained separately as diagnostics

environment.criterion: Preserve the tall, open workshop volume, perimeter equipment bays and central islands of benches, with broad circulation space between them.
Maintain credible relative scale among the high walls, loading opening, tall storage racks, standing-height benches and industrial machinery.
Match the utilitarian atmosphere: daylight patches, fluorescent fixtures, muted gray surfaces, warm timber, orange shelving and localized red equipment.

features.criterion: Tall rectangular hall with exposed roof framing and extensive uninterrupted floor space.
Visible blockwork courses, steel columns and pale roof beams beneath corrugated roof panels.
Gray masonry and dusty concrete floor show stains, scuffs and uneven coloration.
Wall-mounted strip lights, surface conduits and horizontal timber mounting rails follow the equipment perimeter.
A row of tall, narrow bandsaws contrasts with broad, low woodworking machines and their projecting tables.
Bandsaws have upper box housings, slender cutting openings, small horizontal tables and enclosed pedestal bases.
The large saw station has an extended sliding table, guide rails and a raised blade guard.
Off-white and gray painted housings combine with dark tables, exposed metal rails and small colored controls.
High open shelving frames the storage corner, with upright timber clustered between and beside racks.
Perforated gray steel uprights carry orange horizontal beams and several open shelf levels.
Long boards lie horizontally overhead; mixed narrow offcuts stand vertically and large sheets lean nearby.
Pale unfinished wood, rough sheet goods, cardboard cartons and colored parts bins form a varied storage palette.
Two distinct working stations sit within a broader arrangement of central bench islands and wall-side work surfaces.
Reference benches combine thick timber tops with either substantial wooden legs and stretchers or slender dark metal frames.
Worn timber surfaces, painted cabinet bodies and metal fixtures retain the workshop's practical, used appearance.
A tall, broad loading opening occupies the masonry wall and meets the workshop floor.
The photographed door has vertically divided gray metal panels with prominent repeated diagonal lattice bracing.

targets.label: Loading door and connected outdoor bay

features.criterion: Large cylindrical ducts run overhead and along the machinery wall, branching into vertical drops.
Segmented elbows, junctions and ribbed flexible hoses visibly connect the duct network to equipment.
A tall rectangular extraction enclosure anchors the corner behind the large saw station.
Reflective galvanized metal contrasts with translucent pale hoses and the dull masonry background.
The reference handling vehicle has a compact red lower body, very tall narrow mast and two long low forward prongs.
A rear tiller handle, paired fork assembly and small floor-level wheels make its handling purpose legible.
Red painted bodywork contrasts with black lower trim, dark mast components and worn metal forks.
